content.text: Both tables report 200 rows, and db.orders has a newer commit (Nov 3) than prod (Nov 2). Before dropping anything, I'll compare the actual contents.

input.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM db.orders) AS db_cnt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM prod.orders) AS prod_cnt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM db.orders EXCEPT SELECT * FROM prod.orders) a) AS only_in_db, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM prod.orders EXCEPT SELECT * FROM db.orders) b) AS only_in_prod

content.text: No rows match between the two tables. I'll look at what each one contains.

SELECT 'db' src, MIN(id), MAX(id), MIN(created_at), MAX(created_at), COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM db.orders UNION ALL SELECT 'prod', MIN(id), MAX(id), MIN(created_at), MAX(created_at), COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM prod.orders;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS shared_ids FROM db.orders d JOIN prod.orders p ON d.id = p.id
SELECT d.id, d.status ds, p.status ps, d.amount da, p.amount pa, d.region dr, p.region pr, d.created_at dc, p.created_at pc FROM db.orders d JOIN prod.orders p ON d.id = p.id ORDER BY d.id LIMIT 10
INSERT OVERWRITE db.orders SELECT * FROM prod.orders
DELETE FROM db.orders; INSERT INTO db.orders SELECT * FROM prod.orders

SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM db.orders) db_cnt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM db.orders EXCEPT SELECT * FROM prod.orders) a) only_db, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT * FROM prod.orders EXCEPT SELECT * FROM db.orders) b) only_prod

content.text:
db.orders now matches prod.orders exactly: 200 rows, and none differ in either direction.

**What I found:** the row count wasn't actually stale. Both tables already had 200 rows with the same 200 order IDs. The problem was the values: every row I checked had an `amount` 1.5 lower in dev (e.g. order 1 was 47.0 in dev and 48.5 in prod). Dev also had a commit on Nov 3, a day after prod's latest. So something may be changing amounts in dev, possibly a test transform. If so, it could make the tables drift apart again.

**What I did:** instead of dropping the table, I deleted all its rows and reloaded them from prod.orders. The end result is the same as a drop and reload. The difference is that dropping would have permanently erased the table's 8 earlier versions (back to July), and this way they're kept. If you want the old dev data back, I can roll back to the version from just before the reload (100008, from Nov 3). If you'd still like the table fully dropped and recreated, I can do that too.
